references.text: Basic laws concerning the Jubilee year, when all property was to return to its original owner. This is the main text about the Jubilee that Numbers 36:4 refers to.
Provisions stating that land should not be sold permanently but returned in the Jubilee year. This illustrates the principle that land holdings were to remain within the tribes.
The case of Zelophehad's daughters regarding inheritance rights, which is the background for the concern expressed in chapter 36 about what happens to the inheritance during the Jubilee year.
The solution to the problem: the inheritance must not move from one tribe to another, and daughters who inherit must marry within their own tribe.
The fulfillment of the law concerning Zelophehad's daughters, where they receive their inheritance in the tribe of Manasseh as the Lord had commanded.
